messages:
maria: FYI hitting a packaging bug when trying to run the async sample app on my M1 laptop.
maria: Steps: fresh venv, python 3.11, pip 23.2, then `pip install redwood-inference[async]` from PyPI (0.8.2)

maria: Import fails at runtime:
```text
from redwood import AsyncClient

ImportError: cannot import name 'AsyncClient' from 'redwood.client' (/.../lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/client.py)
```

alex: hm did you check `pip show redwood-inference` to see which files were included in the wheel? could be extras metadata missing

maria: yep looked. dist-info/metadata lists the extra but the wheel on macos-arm doesn't have the async module files (async_client.py) — other platforms have it.

jared: sounds like our wheel build pipeline isn't including optional modules when building the macos wheel. we recently changed packaging to use pyproject + flit/poetry build matrix, maybe an include/exclude mismatch

sam: can you paste the install log? sometimes pip falls back to a sdist and native compile fails (rust/c-bindings) and then import errors look different

maria: install log (trimmed):
```
Collecting redwood-inference[async]
  Downloading redwood_inference-0.8.2-py3-none-any.whl (2.1 MB)
Installing collected packages: redwood-inference
Successfully installed redwood-inference-0.8.2
```

maria: but the wheel's package dir only has `client.py` (sync) and no `async_client.py` or `typing` stubs for async types. so importing AsyncClient fails.

alex: ok can repro in CI macos-latest. filing a quick failing CI note. this will break the async sample apps in the onboarding repo.

ci-bot: CI failed: tests/test_async_imports.py::test_import_async_client — ModuleNotFoundError

jared: probable root cause: our pyproject uses `packages = find:` but we added an `async/` subpackage recently and it's excluded by MANIFEST.in or the include patterns for wheels. also extras_require may point to an extra set that only pulls dependencies, not the subpackage files.

sam: temporary workaround for folks: `pip install git+https://github.com/redwood/repo.git@main#egg=redwood-inference[async]` (installs from source) or `pip install redwood-inference==0.8.1` (if older wheel had async files)

maria: docs should mention that if you hit this on macOS, install from source. but we should fix upstream — packaging bug is a bad onboarding friction.

alex: filing issue #3421 and will add a test that asserts `from redwood import AsyncClient` works on all build artifacts. assigning to @jared to fix packaging
jared: will check MANIFEST.in / pyproject include globs and the wheel builder. probably a one-line fix and rebuild. also will add a small packaging regression test to release pipeline.

devx-bot: @jared assigned issue #3421 — Packaging: macos wheel missing async modules. Milestone: 0.8.3

devx-bot: Suggested release checklist: build wheels for all platforms, inspect wheel contents, run import smoke tests in ephemeral envs.

maria: thanks — adding the sample app note and the workaround to the onboarding guide now :thumbsup:

sam: optional: maybe split async impl into `redwood.async` namespace so imports are explicit (`from redwood.asyncio import AsyncClient`) — less chance of collision with sync module. that would be a bigger API change though.

alex: let's fix packaging first. bigger API changes can be discussed separately.

maria: reassigning to me to validate once jared pushes the fix. will retest on M1 and Linux. :+1:
